rulers.name: Qutb-ud-din Mubarak Shah
rulers.note: Crowned 14 April 1316, killed on the night of 9 July 1320 (Mubarak Shah page). Khusrau Khan, who murdered him and reigned until Ghazi Malik's victory at Lahrawat on 6 September 1320, is not in the infobox table.

Bengal is taken out of every Khalji shape: no page opened gives a Khalji conquest of Bengal. The Tughlaq dynasty page has Ghiyath al-Din 'expand eastwards into Bengal by attacking Shamsuddin Firoz Shah, which he did over 1324-1325' and the Muhammad bin Tughluq page has Munger 'annexed' from Bengal in 1330; the Mamluk dossier (sa-04-a) has Bengal independent under Bughra Khan's line from 1287. Cliopatria's shapes hold 285 (1294, 1305) and 647 (1314) of Bengal's 804 cells. [fx-03, 2026-11-01: the Cliopatria outline's cover of Karnat Tirhut, Bundi and Jaipur land is taken out. region.text: the Delhi sultanate Jalaluddin took in the Khalji Revolution: the Cliopatria 1294 Khalji outline without Bengal and Ranthambore; without the land of the Karnat kingdom of Tirhut, Bundi and Jaipur (Dhundhar), which no page gives to Delhi (fx-03)

ledger.note: 1290: Jalal ud-Din Firuz Khalji founds the Khalji dynasty at Delhi. Infobox 'Khalji Revolution: 13 June 1290'; the last Mamluk, Muiz ud din Qaiqabad, 'was killed in the Kailu-gheri Palace during the coup known as the Khalji Revolution' and Jalaluddin 'ascended the throne of Delhi in January 1290' (the page's two dates differ; the Delhi Sultanate infobox gives 'Khalji Revolution 1 February - 13 June 1290'). The page names the city, not a frontier. [fx-03: the founding outline no longer covers the Karnat, Bundi and Jaipur land (see keyframes).]

1298: Mongol invaders hold Sivistan. 'Zafar Khan defeated the invaders and recaptured Sivistan' (1298-99, Sindh); before it the Mongols had raided the Punjab in 1297-98 and 'Alauddin's forces, led by Ulugh Khan, defeated the Mongols on 6 February 1298'. The page calls the Sivistan force 'another Mongol army (possibly Neguderi fugitives)'; Duwa is named only for the 1299 march on Delhi (counterpart corrected from chagatai-khanate by reviewer sa-04-b).

1299: Zafar Khan recaptures Sivistan. The page dates the Sindh war '1298-99' without a day; in the same year Duwa 'sent a Mongol force led by Qutlugh Khwaja to conquer Delhi' and Zafar Khan was killed at the battle of Kili while Qutlugh Khwaja died on the retreat (raid, no ground held).

region.text: the fort of Ranthambore and its lands

ledger.note: 1301: Ranthambore falls to Alauddin. 'Alauddin personally took charge of the siege operations, and conquered the fort in July 1301', after Nusrat Khan was killed there.
1303: Alauddin takes Chittor. 'He himself led another army to conquer Chittor'; the siege lasted eight months (Khalji page: 'Chittorgarh (1303)').

region.text: Gujarat, the Vaghela kingdom, as far as the Cliopatria 1305 shape holds it

ledger.note: 1304: Gujarat is annexed. 'A second invasion in 1304 annexed the Vaghela kingdom', after the raid of early 1299 by Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan. The Khalji page dates the conquest to 1299 ('in 1299 Nusrat Khan was sent to conquer Gujarat itself, where he defeated its Solanki king'); the Alauddin page's two-step account is followed.

1305: Malwa falls. 'In 1305, he launched an invasion of Malwa', which ended with the death of the Paramara king Mahalakadeva; Ayn al-Mulk Multani became the province's governor (Khalji page: 'Malwa(1305)').
1308: Malik Kafur marches on Devagiri. 'Malik Kafur invaded around 1308 and achieved an easy victory' (the Khalji page quotes 'He took Devagiri - the capital of the Yadava - in 1307').
1308: Ramachandra submits, and the war ends the same year.
1308: the Yadavas become Delhi's tributaries. Ramachandra, who had promised tribute in 1296 and stopped paying it, 'agreed to become a lifelong vassal'.
1308: Siwana falls. 'He personally directed the siege in August-September 1308. The ruler Sitaladeva was killed in November 1308.'

1310: Malik Kafur besieges Warangal. 'Prataparudra submitted after a month-long siege' (the Khalji page puts the capture of Warangal in 1308 with the sentence 'captured Warangal, overthrew the Hoysala Empire south of the Krishna River and raided Madurai').
1310: Prataparudra submits after the siege.
1310: the Kakatiyas become tributaries. 'After the 1310 siege, Prataparudra agreed to become a tributary.'

1311: Malik Kafur attacks Dwarasamudra. 'Ballala III negotiated a truce after a short siege'; the same year Kafur raided as far as Madurai ('Vira and Sundara' fled their capital), a raid that left no tributary.
1311: Ballala III makes terms after a short siege.
1311: the Hoysalas become tributaries. 'In 1311, Ballala III agreed to surrender wealth and become a tributary.'
1311: Jalore falls. 'In 1311, Alauddin's general Malik Kamaluddin Gurg captured the Jalore fort after defeating and killing Kanhadadeva.'
1313: the Yadava tribute ends in annexation (see the gain of the same year).

region.text: the Yadava kingdom of Devagiri, governed by Malik Kafur

ledger.note: 1313: Devagiri is annexed. 'Kafur invaded again in 1313 and became governor.' The page does not describe the frontier; the whole Yadava outline is my reading.

1316: Devagiri breaks away. 'The Yadavas seized Devagiri and declared independence under Harapaladeva'; the page gives no date (Kafur left in 1315, Alauddin died on 4 January 1316), so the year is a bridging judgment.

1317: Mubarak Shah retakes Devagiri. 'In April 1317, during the second year of his reign, Mubarak Shah marched to Devagiri with a large army'; most local chiefs accepted his suzerainty and Malik Yaklakhi was made governor.

1320: the Kakatiya tribute ends with the dynasty. The pages opened give the 1310 submission and say Mubarak Shah 'extended control' over Warangal, not when the tribute stopped; Tughlaq armies besiege Warangal in 1321 and 1323 (Tughlaq pages).
1320: the Hoysala tribute is closed with the dynasty; the pages opened do not say when the Hoysalas stopped paying.

region.text: the whole sultanate (the Cliopatria 1314 outline without Bengal plus Devagiri), passing to Ghazi Malik's Tughlaq dynasty

ledger.note: 1320: the Khalji dynasty ends. Mubarak Shah was killed on the night of 9 July 1320 by Khusrau Khan, whom Ghazi Malik defeated at Lahrawat on 6 September 1320 (Delhi Sultanate page); 'Upon becoming sultan, Ghazi Malik renamed himself Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq' (Khalji page). The Khalji page's infobox says 'Disestablished: 1 May 1320'; Cliopatria keeps the row to 1325.

wars.name: Khalji conquest of Gujarat
wars.outcome: Raid in early 1299 (Ulugh Khan, Nusrat Khan), annexation of the Vaghela kingdom in 1304.
wars.note: The Khalji page dates the conquest to 1299.

wars.name: Siege of Ranthambore
wars.outcome: Fort conquered in July 1301 after Nusrat Khan was killed; Alauddin led the siege himself.

wars.name: Siege of Chittorgarh
wars.outcome: Chittor conquered after a siege of eight months.

wars.name: Khalji conquest of Malwa
wars.outcome: Mahalakadeva killed; Malwa a province under Ayn al-Mulk Multani.

wars.name: Khalji conquest of Siwana and Jalore
wars.outcome: Siwana taken in the autumn of 1308 (Sitaladeva killed in November); Jalore captured in 1311 (Kanhadadeva killed).

wars.name: Mongol invasions of India under Alauddin
wars.outcome: Khalji victories at Jaran-Manjur (6 February 1298), over the Sindh raiders (1298-99), at Kili (1299, Zafar Khan killed), at Amroha (1305) and on the Ravi (1306); the siege of Delhi in August 1303 was abandoned. Only Sivistan changed hands, briefly.
wars.note: The Khalji page adds the massacre of Mongols in Delhi in 1311.

wars.name: Malik Kafur's southern campaigns
wars.outcome: Yadavas (1308), Kakatiyas (1310) and Hoysalas (1311) become tributaries; Madurai raided in 1311 without a submission; Devagiri annexed in 1313.
wars.note: The Khalji page gives 1308 for Warangal and the Hoysala defeat and 1307 for Devagiri; the Alauddin page's dates are used.

wars.name: Mubarak Shah's reconquest of Devagiri
wars.outcome: Harapaladeva's rising crushed; Devagiri under a governor again.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the pages give cities, forts and kingdoms, not boundaries. The Rajput forts and the Gujarat and Malwa borders are the nearest to dated lines; the Deccan states are tributaries whose borders are not the sultanate's.

notes: Khalji dynasty: three Cliopatria shapes (1294-1325) reviewed against Khalji dynasty, Alauddin Khalji and Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah, with the Delhi Sultanate page for the infobox areas (1300 about 1.5 M, 1312 about 3.2 M, 1350 about 2.8 M km2). (1) Dates: Cliopatria starts the row in 1294 and ends it in 1325; the pages give 13 June 1290 and 9 July 1320 (infobox 'Disestablished: 1 May 1320'; Lahrawat 6 September 1320). 1290-1293 is carried by a new keyframe, 1321-1325 by the Tughlaq dossier. (2) Bengal: removed from all three shapes (reasoning in the 1290 keyframe); the Mamluk dossier gives Bengal to the Balbani line from 1287. Sind: kept, supported by Sivistan 1298-99 only. Unverified: page budget: the Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Bihar cells added by the 1314 shape. (3) The Mamluk dossier hands over 'Mamluk 1285 minus Bengal' in 1290 while Cliopatria's Khalji outline is 0.84 M km2 against the Mamluk 1.34 M: the pages here show the Rajput and Malwa lands being conquered only in 1301-1311, so the smaller outline is used; the Mamluk dossier's 1291-1293 keyframe may need the same trim. (4) Page disagreements: Gujarat 1299 (Khalji) against 1304 (Alauddin); Warangal and Dwarasamudra 1308 (Khalji) against 1310 and 1311 (Alauddin); Devagiri 1307 (Khalji, quoting Smith) against 1308 (Alauddin); Jalaluddin's accession January 1290 against 13 June 1290 (infobox); end 1 May 1320 (infobox) against 9 July 1320 (Mubarak Shah page). (5) Counterparts that need dossiers or slugs: chahamanas-of-ranastambhapura (Ranthambore, the slug the Chauhan dossier names), chahamanas-of-jalor (Siwana and Jalore). chaulukya-dynasty, guhilas-of-mewar, paramara-dynasty, yadava-dynasty, kakatiya-dynasty and hoysala-kingdom have dossiers from sa-03 whose end years agree (1304, 1303, 1305, 1317, 1323, 1343). (6) Not modelled, page silent or no ground held: Alauddin's raids on Bhilsa (1293) and Devagiri (1296), the Multan campaign (November 1296), Kafur's Madurai raid (1311), Alauddin's 1296 coup (20 July) and coronation (21 October), Khusrau Khan's months in 1320. (7) The Delhi Sultanate dynasties (Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi) are one state in the Wikipedia sense; the colour agent should keep one hue (family india) for them. (8) Region names the gazetteer lacks: coordinates are used for Ranthambore, Siwana, Jalore and Sivistan (Sehwan).
